clue.text: Starters in Italian hardly cooked deceive German, sending back dumplings

indicators.note: sending back tells us to read the whole string of collected letters from right to left
starters are the opening letters of the words that follow

parts.note: to con someone is to deceive or swindle them

explanation.surface: A cook rushes undercooked Italian starters and cheats a German diner, who sends the dumplings back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sending back' reverses IHC + CON + G, the starters' initials plus the con and the German, all in one go.
explanation.definitionFit: Small Italian dumplings made from potato or semolina are served much like pasta.

clue.text: Training courses lifted the lid on education

indicators.note: lifted means raised, so in a down entry the pieces read upwards

parts.note: a rut is a course, as in a groove a wheel follows
a run is a course, as in a ski run

indicators.note: the lid is the top letter, the first of the following word

explanation.surface: Training courses gave people a first look at education.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courses' gives two words, RUT and RUN; 'lifted' turns both upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Upbringing and schooling help a child grow, which is a kind of rearing or instruction.

clue.text: Loud sound signal cues packing up

indicators.note: up means read upwards, reversed in this down entry
packing means the clue words hold the letters inside them

explanation.surface: A loud signal tells everyone it is time to pack up.
explanation.definitionFit: A clang is a ringing metallic noise, like a bell or dropped pan.

clue.text: A filling in hot recipe, is it?

definitions.text: A filling in hot recipe, is it?

indicators.note: filling in means the A goes inside the other letters

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
R is short for recipe, from the Latin on prescriptions
taken as written
it is sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: Asks whether something used as a filling in a spicy recipe is this paste.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a spicy paste used in North African cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiery North African chilli paste is often stirred into or spread through hot dishes.

clue.text: To get a better position, White's third play captures pawn with rook

indicators.note: third picks out the third letter of the word White's
captures means one piece takes the others inside it, as in chess

parts.note: a move is a play in a game
P is the chess notation for a pawn
R is the chess notation for a rook

explanation.surface: Chess commentary: White's third move takes a pawn with the rook to gain a stronger position.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess setting is a cover; 'captures' is a container signal, putting P and R inside MOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something or oneself better is to advance or upgrade one's standing.

clue.text: The first person to entrap a Group One flyer

indicators.note: to entrap means to catch inside, so the first piece holds the others

parts.note: me is the first-person pronoun
GP is an abbreviation for group
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A trap set for a Group One racehorse, which turns out to be a flyer.
explanation.definitionFit: A black-and-white crow, fond of shiny things, is a common bird.

clue.text: Jargon so bemusing, Henry's order in Indian?

indicators.note: bemusing means confusing, so these letters are muddled

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry is baffled by curry-house jargon when ordering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' means an Indian restaurant, so the definition is a dish one orders there.
explanation.definitionFit: This aromatic lamb curry is a staple dish on British Indian restaurant menus.

clue.text: Serving of 7 is only meat

indicators.note: a serving is a portion taken from the words, here the number written out as seven

parts.note: 7 is spelt out as the word seven for its letters

explanation.surface: A portion of the curry at 7 is the only meat on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: '7' looks like a cross-reference to the curry at 7 down, but here it is simply the word seven: seVEN IS ONly.
explanation.definitionFit: Deer flesh is a game meat served roasted or in stews.

clue.text: Referring to revolutionary, if not horrific period of history

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned around and overthrown, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: or means if not, as in pay or else

explanation.surface: Talk of a revolutionary era that was, if not horrific, at least grim.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at the French Revolution, which is in fact the answer's period.
explanation.definitionFit: The bloody purge of 1793 to 1794 in revolutionary France killed thousands by guillotine.

clue.text: Essentially, lifting legendary setter's gold wheels is a strain

indicators.note: lifting means taking these pieces away, out of the longer name

parts.note: Araucaria was the legendary Guardian setter John Graham
AU is the chemical symbol for gold
wheels is slang for a car

explanation.surface: A puzzling sentence about the famous setter's golden car being stolen, which proves a strain.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria (the late John Graham) was a revered Guardian setter. Lifting AUCAR from the middle of his name leaves the essential A-R ... I-A, hence 'Essentially'.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a tune or melody, and an operatic solo song is one such air.

clue.text: Instigating new action executing the picking of plums?

indicators.note: executing means beheading, so the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a greengage is a kind of plum, so gathering them is jokingly greengaging

explanation.surface: Starting a new campaign by carrying out a plum harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the made-up verb for gathering greengages; executing it removes its head G.
explanation.definitionFit: To take up a fight or hire again is to start fresh combat or employment once more.

clue.text: Book 16s gutted about Elbow missing lead

indicators.note: about means the outer letters go round the inner piece
gutted means the insides of the word are removed, leaving only its ends

parts.note: 16s refers to the answer at 16 across, made plural

indicators.note: missing lead means losing the first letter

parts.note: to elbow someone is to nudge them

explanation.surface: A grumpy note that nightclubs are hollowed out and the band Elbow has lost its lead singer.
explanation.walkthrough: Elbow is a British rock band, which makes the surface look like music news. 'gutted' leaves just the outside letters J and S.
explanation.definitionFit: The seventh book of the Old Testament tells of the leaders of Israel before the kings.

clue.text: This Alec displaying genuine class in cast

definitions.text: This Alec displaying genuine class in cast

indicators.note: cast means thrown into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tribute to a famous actor whose genuine class shone through every cast he joined.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'genuine class' are the answer plus those of ALEC; the whole clue is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Alec, star of Kind Hearts and Coronets and Star Wars, was a celebrated English film actor.

clue.text: Set One was scuppered when the rains came

indicators.note: scuppered means wrecked, so these letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A tennis set or cricket match was washed out once the rains arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: In tropical climates the monsoon months are the rainy part of the year.

clue.text: Surely not as address for the Hammers? It's taken off

parts.note: the Communist symbol pairs the hammer with the sickle
ave is a Latin form of greeting or address, and also short for avenue

explanation.surface: Joking that a street name for West Ham fans could hardly be this.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hammers is the nickname of West Ham football club; the hammer's partner on the Soviet flag is the sickle. 'Surely not' warns the address is a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Time off work granted because of illness is a period away from one's job.

clue.text: Quickly set down outside fashionable nightclub, maybe

indicators.note: outside means the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: to jot something is to write it down quickly
in means fashionable, as in the in thing

explanation.surface: Someone scribbles a note outside a trendy nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint is informal slang for a venue such as a club or bar, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Such a change would make this thick soupy liquor

parts.words: Such a change would make this thick
parts.note: read as instructions, the answer says change S into CK, which turns the word this into thick

explanation.surface: A cooking tip: this change will thicken the soup.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as S TO CK: swapping the final S of 'this' for CK gives 'thick'.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquor here means the liquid from cooking meat or bones, which is the base for soup.

clue.text: Couple setting up broadcast in personal dedication

indicators.note: in means the reversed piece goes inside the dedication

parts.note: a dedication to oneself would read to me

indicators.note: setting up means raising, read upwards in a down entry

parts.note: to sow seed is to broadcast it, scattering widely

explanation.surface: A pair setting up a broadcast with a personal dedication on air.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of people together, as on a date, form a duo.

clue.text: That man's just robbed me of the tips off trolley!

indicators.note: off one's trolley means crazy, so these letters go haywire into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone shouts after a thief who has just grabbed things from a trolley.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the classic shout of a victim calling for help to catch a robber.

clue.text: Perhaps The Ancient Mariner's stopping for an ancient card game?

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
Coleridge's poem is The Rime of the Ancient Mariner, an example of a rime

explanation.surface: Wondering whether Coleridge's old sailor stops by for an old card game.
explanation.walkthrough: Coleridge wrote The Rime of the Ancient Mariner, so the poem is 'perhaps' a rime.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a gambling game with cards popular in Tudor England, a forerunner of poker.

clue.text: Murderer's chopped up diminutive missing women round Serpentine

indicators.note: round means the first piece wraps around the second
missing means the next letter is taken out

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small

indicators.note: up means read upwards in this down entry
chopped means the end is cut off

parts.note: a murderer is a killer

explanation.surface: A murderer is dismembered and dumped by tiny women round the Serpentine lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The Serpentine is a lake in London's Hyde Park, but here it is an adjective, snakelike.
explanation.definitionFit: Snakelike and slippery in shape, as a long sinuous fish is.

clue.text: Open tank to replace Japanese icon

indicators.note: to replace means one letter is swapped for another piece

parts.note: a door left ajar is slightly open
a vat is a large tank

explanation.surface: An open tank is installed to replace a Japanese icon.
explanation.definitionFit: In computing, the small picture representing a user online is a profile image.

clue.text: Nothing left between Romeo and his Juliet but the bigger prize

indicators.note: between means these letters go in the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Juliet is Romeo's sweetheart, his lover
nothing is zero, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Nothing remains between the star-crossed lovers but a bigger prize.
explanation.walkthrough: In a lottery, an unwon jackpot is carried over to the next draw, making it bigger.
explanation.definitionFit: An unclaimed lottery jackpot carried forward to the next draw grows larger.

clue.text: Current partner with wheels seeking the highest standards

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
in the phrase wheels and deals, deals is the partner of wheels

explanation.surface: A wheeler-dealer partner of the moment is looking for the best of everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Principles or perfect models to aim at are the loftiest standards one can hold.

clue.text: Bloody Viz goes up and down on it!

indicators.note: goes up means the letters read upwards in this down entry

parts.note: red is the colour of blood
viz and i.e. both mean that is

explanation.surface: The comic Viz goes up and down with its rude humour.
explanation.walkthrough: Viz is a British adult comic, but here it means 'namely'. The definition is cryptic: this duck has its famous down on it.
explanation.definitionFit: This sea duck grows soft breast feathers once used to fill quilts.

clue.text: What one versed in dodges does right in order to crack what's typical of Philistine

definitions.text: What one versed in dodges does

indicators.note: to crack means to break into, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: a philistine is someone with no taste for the arts
OK means in order, all right

explanation.surface: A skiver does the right thing to break through a philistine's typical attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: A Philistine is someone uncultured, so 'what's typical' of one is no taste.
explanation.definitionFit: A shirker skilled at avoiding work does no work at all, the idiom says.

clue.text: One's pathetic GP coming over all sanctimonious

parts.note: a GP, a family doctor, is addressed as Dr

indicators.note: coming over means the next word turns round, read backwards

parts.note: pi is informal for pious or sanctimonious

explanation.surface: A feeble family doctor suddenly turns all holier-than-thou.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming over all' is an idiom for suddenly acting a certain way; 'all' is just a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: A drip is a weak, ineffectual person, someone feeble and wet.

clue.text: It's jolly good fun returning to your little bar

indicators.note: returning means the letters run back the other way

parts.note: YR is a short form of your
a lever is a metal bar used to prise things

explanation.surface: An invitation: it's great fun coming back to your cosy little pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The little bar sounds like a pub, but it is a crowbar or lever.
explanation.definitionFit: Merrymaking and lively festivity are a cheerful kind of fun.

clue.text: Youngster from Australia secures place for Ashes tour

indicators.note: secures means holds inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a joey is a young kangaroo
an urn holds ashes; the Ashes cricket trophy is a tiny urn

explanation.surface: A young Australian cricketer secures a place on the Ashes tour.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the England-Australia cricket series, whose trophy is a small urn.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip or voyage from place to place is a tour or expedition.
